definitions.explanation: A gender-neutral term for one's husband or wife, often used when speaking about one's own spouse or someone else's.

examples.japanese: {連|つ}れ{合|あ}いと{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}ってきた。
examples.english: I went on a trip with my spouse.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{連|つ}れ{合|あ}いを{亡|な}くした。
examples.english: They lost their spouse of many years.

examples.japanese: お{連|つ}れ{合|あ}いは{お元気|おげんき}ですか。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: From {連|つ}れ{合|あ}う 'to accompany each other.' Literally 'companion.'

REGISTER: Slightly formal and respectful. Often used when referring to someone else's spouse with お{連|つ}れ{合|あ}い.

NUANCE: A warm, traditional term that emphasizes the companionship aspect of marriage. Gender-neutral, making it useful when the speaker doesn't want to specify husband or wife.

CONTRAST WITH OTHER TERMS:
・{夫|おっと} / {妻|つま} - formal for own spouse (documents, etc.)
・{旦那|だんな} / {奥|おく}さん - common colloquial terms
・{主人|しゅじん} / {家内|かない} - traditional, becoming less common
・パートナー - modern, gender-neutral loanword
